risks: Minimal physical risk; the risk is privacy harm from reading identifiable social work notes, which contain sensitive family information.
consent: Consent is impracticable for 480 past discharges, some of whom have died; the research ethics board will be asked for a waiver of consent for secondary use under minimal risk, with notice on the hospital's research transparency page.
data: Readers work in the hospital's secure environment; the analysis file holds no names, hospital numbers or free text, only coded variables; the linkage key is held by the informatics team and destroyed after analysis.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: attendance depends on carers' work, transport and language, so families in deprived areas, working carers and families needing interpreters may be under-represented among attended meetings. Results will be reported by area deprivation quintile and by in-person versus telephone attendance, and any recommendation will address access to meetings, not only whether they are held.
effectiveness: The study informs whether standard meetings for everyone over 75 are worth social work time; a precise null result is as useful as a positive one.
efficiency: Uses existing notes and 120 approved hours; no patient contact.
costs: Social worker and informatics time within existing roles.
grants: None needed; a positive result would support an application for a trial of structured family meetings.
partnerships: Medical director's office (policy question), informatics team (sampling and linkage), two carer representatives from the hospital's carers' forum (exposure definition and interpretation), and the ward discharge coordinators.
rebPath: Full review by the hospital research ethics board for secondary use of identifiable social work notes with a waiver of consent, following ICH-GCP and Declaration of Helsinki principles; the board has not yet been asked, so the gate is unknown and no note is read before approval.
limitations: Residual confounding by family engagement; readmissions to other hospitals missed; notes may not record telephone attendance consistently.
summary: Secondary use of sensitive notes with a waiver request, equity reporting by deprivation and mode of attendance, and an ethics gate still unknown.
